title: How to Manage Stock in a Small Shop: A Practical Guide
description: A practical guide to managing stock in a small shop: count what you have, track what you sell, reorder on time and avoid losses.
author: Bizora Team

faq.question: How often should a small shop count its stock?
faq.answer: There is no single schedule that works for every business. Fast-moving or high-value products may need more frequent checks, while other products may be reviewed less often. The important thing is to establish a regular stock-counting routine.

faq.question: What should I record when buying stock?
faq.answer: At minimum, record the product, quantity received and relevant purchase information. Keeping the purchase or cost price can also help you understand the financial side of your stock.

faq.question: How do I know when my stock is running low?
faq.answer: Set a minimum quantity for important products and monitor when the available stock approaches that level. A low-stock alert can make this easier.

faq.question: Why doesn't my physical stock match my records?
faq.answer: Differences can result from unrecorded sales, damaged products, theft, counting errors, incorrect stock entries or other stock movements. Investigating the difference is important before simply changing the recorded quantity.

faq.question: Is a notebook enough for managing stock?
faq.answer: A notebook can work for a very small operation with few products and transactions. As the business grows, digital tools can make it easier to organize products, record sales and monitor stock.

faq.question: Can a POS system help with stock management?
faq.answer: Yes. When a POS system connects sales records with inventory records, recording a sale can also update the corresponding stock quantity. This can reduce the amount of manual stock tracking required.
